newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down on Wednesday on profit-taking with the short-term market trend unclear due to the failure of the London Metal Exchange to hold to gains made earlier this week, traders said.
The most active June 1997 contract ended at 23,550 yuan ($2,839) per tonne, losing 50 yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 23,650, hitting a low of 23,460.
March was unchanged at 23,150 yuan, April fell 120 to 23,360, May 40 to 23,520 and July 80 to 23,500. August was unchanged at 23,550.
Combined volume fell to 45,870 tonnes from 47,800.
Copper opened higher and profit-taking pushed prices steadily down for most of the session.
"Profit-taking dominated today's trading because investors are unwilling to let possible sharp falls erase their current gains," one trader said.
"Poor performance on the London Metal Exchange hurt the confidence of long position holders, as a result of which most of them stayed on the sidelines," he said.
Traders said copper would fall further on a technical correction.
"Copper is likely to continue to fall in the next few days because the market needs more time to digest heavy gains accumulated over the past two weeks," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended down across the board. March fell 150 to 16,000 yuan per tonne, April 150 to 16,300, May 170 to 16,610 and June 180 to 16,800.
Combined volume fell to 3,090 tonnes from 4,700.
